situation.person: Employed/breastfeeding mother in the final month of maternity leave, dreading the return - pumping logistics, the morning hand-off, supply drop fear, guilt math - with no plan beyond a start date
situation.specific_situation: Return date is ~30 days out; nothing is prepared: no freezer bank, no pump-space agreement, no childcare backup, no morning system; she oscillates between denial and 2am panic
situation.timeframe: 15 days before return through first 15 days back
situation.trigger: The calendar: leave ends on a fixed date
situation.problem: She has no operating system for the transition, so week one back becomes supply crash + workplace embarrassment + evening meltdowns + guilt that eats her
situation.failed_attempt: Tried to 'just wing it and see'; or over-bought gadgets without a system; asked other mothers and got contradictory war stories
situation.emotional_stake: She fears losing her milk, her edge at work, and her bond with the baby simultaneously - and believes dropping any one ball proves she can't have both career and motherhood
situation.desired_transformation: A dated 30-day operating system: rights-backed workplace ask locked, feeding lane chosen, freezer bank built, childcare drilled, morning/evening anchors running - so week one back is execution, not improvisation

failed_attempts: Waiting for HR to volunteer support

new_capabilities: Negotiates adjustments from legal footing in writing
Executes three daily anchors (hand-off, blocks, bridge)
systems_created: Feeding-lane choice + logistics card for caregiver
remaining_limits: Some employers still resist - escalation takes time
Feelings need their own support channels
evidence_of_change: All before-dates hit or consciously re-planned

mechanism.core_mechanism: Project-management applied to a life transition: dated single-move days remove overwhelm; legal-footing scripts convert hope into entitlements; three anchors compress daily decisions into routines
mechanisms: Anchor routines reduce decision fatigue at known failure points (morning, workday, 5pm)
mechanism.why_it_should_work: Transition failure concentrates at predictable nodes (logistics untested, accommodations unwritten, evenings unplanned); a dated OS addresses each node before it fires

evidence_basis.claim: US: PUMP Act requires reasonable break time + private non-bathroom space ~1yr post-birth for nearly all employees; PWFA adds accommodation duties
evidence_basis.source: US DOL Wage & Hour Division PUMP-at-work materials (2024); EEOC PWFA

evidence_basis.claim: UK: no statutory pumping breaks but Equality Act 2010 protects against breastfeeding discrimination; HSE expects clean private space (never toilets); 52-week maternity leave
evidence_basis.source: Maternity Action; NHS employer guidance; HSE

evidence_basis.claim: Nigeria: Labour Act s.54 floor of 12 weeks maternity leave at >=50% pay
evidence_basis.source: Nigeria Labour Act s54(1) - verified correction in project memory

evidence_basis.claim: Expressed-milk storage: refrigerate ~4 days / freeze best within 3 months; thaw oldest-first, never microwave
Mastitis signs (red hot wedge, fever, flu-feel) need same-day clinician contact while keeping milk moving

transformation_path.objective: Confirm dates; choose feeding lane via Decision Card
Freezer bank + childcare lock + trial run
Written employer adjustment; Morning Drill x2; bag built
Three anchors daily; Sunday reset; Wednesday fix-one

failure_point_map.rescue_protocol: Audit missed blocks; add early-morning or night pump temporarily; hydration/latch check; lactation line if trend continues
Re-state in writing citing law/guidance; propose concrete coverage plan; escalate HR -> agency route per country card
Re-run Night-before station checklist ruthlessly for 3 days; cut ONE morning step permanently
Bridge ritual moved earlier; partner takes first 30 min post-arrival; feed in calm dim room

failure_point_map.scenario: Red hot wedge + fever + flu feeling
failure_point_map.rescue_protocol: Clinician SAME DAY; keep milk flowing gently; warm compress before feeds, cold after
Clinical support route + crisis numbers; not a discipline problem

first_win.action: Send the Employer Ask email from Script 1 today - dated, written, rights-cited - and put '+2 bags tonight' on the freezer bank log
first_win.observable_change: A dated written request exists and the freezer bank counter shows its first entries

success_indicators: >=80% planned pump blocks taken in weeks 1-2
tsm.success_threshold: 60%+ completers meet >=3 of 4 indicators at Day-15-back review
tsm.measurement_method: Milestone tracker + daily block/hand-off ticks + Day-15 structured review
tsm.incomplete_progress_interpretation: Missed milestones are rescheduled not mourned; only silent skipping counts against - visible replanning keeps progress intact
tsm.next_action_on_miss: Wednesday fix-one-thing targets the specific broken anchor; employer issues re-escalate via written path

maintenance.maintenance_system: After day 15: weekly Sunday reset continues until routine feels boring (that's success)
maintenance.relapse_protocol: Chaos relapse (travel/growth spurts): reinstate night-before station + blocks audit for one week
maintenance.reentry_protocol: Restart at Run phase anchors only; no before-phase guilt

evidence.source: US DOL/EEOC 2024; Maternity Action/NHS/HSE UK; Nigeria Labour Act s54(1)

safety.scope_boundary: Coordinates logistics, rights communication and routines ONLY. Never provides medical advice on mastitis/supply beyond routing to clinicians, never legal representation, never diagnoses PPD.
red_flags: mastitis signs (red hot wedge/fever/flu-feel) = clinician same day
supply collapse across 3+ days = lactation support
persistent hopelessness/dread = clinical support + crisis lines
escalation_rules: Mood crisis -> verified shared crisis list
Workplace rights violations -> documented escalation path per country card

research_disposition.rationale: Flagship #6 (score 79). Narrow window (the 30 days around return) = productizable per original validation; Western-first appeal strong; Nigerian legal facts verified/corrected.
